⚖️ A number almost nobody knows.

In 2025, 77,000 people were granted permission to stay in the UK under Article 8 — the "family life and private life" route. That is about 7% of every visa granted in-country.

Labour's Immigration and Asylum Bill is meant to tighten this up.

The Home Office's OWN impact assessment says it could produce 11,700 more refusals.

That is one in seven. Six out of seven carry on exactly as before. 😐

And it gets worse — the same document concedes that MORE THAN HALF of people whose Article 8 case fails may simply remain in the UK illegally anyway.

To be fair, the Bill does make real changes: narrowing the definition of "family", a good character test, tougher rules for foreign offenders. I am not calling it cosmetic.

But the Commons Library puts it plainly — the Bill "would not attempt to eliminate the ability of migrants to invoke Article 8". And what Article 8 MEANS is decided in Strasbourg, not Westminster.

One last figure that settles the argument: 71% of people newly granted residence rights in 2025 had either entered illegally or overstayed a visa.

Breaking the rules is currently a viable immigration strategy. Fix that. 🇬🇧
